mapper.insert: insert into sys_user (username, password_hash, employee_id, status) values (#{username,jdbcType=VARCHAR}, #{passwordHash,jdbcType=VARCHAR}, #{employeeId,jdbcType=INTEGER}, #{status,jdbcType=TINYINT})
mapper.update: update sys_user set username = #{username,jdbcType=VARCHAR}, password_hash = #{passwordHash,jdbcType=VARCHAR}, employee_id = #{employeeId,jdbcType=INTEGER}, status = #{status,jdbcType=TINYINT}, created_at = #{createdAt,jdbcType=TIMESTAMP} where user_id = #{userId,jdbcType=INTEGER}
mapper.select: select user_id, username, password_hash, employee_id, status, created_at from sys_user

where.if: AND ( u.username LIKE CONCAT('%', #{keyword,jdbcType=VARCHAR}, '%') OR e.full_name LIKE CONCAT('%', #{keyword,jdbcType=VARCHAR}, '%') OR e.employee_code LIKE CONCAT('%', #{keyword,jdbcType=VARCHAR}, '%') )

mapper.select: select count(*) from sys_user u left join employee e on e.employee_id = u.employee_id

select u.user_id as userId, u.username as username, u.status as status, r.role_name as roleName, u.employee_id as employeeId, e.employee_code as employeeCode, e.full_name as employeeName, u.created_at as createdAt from sys_user u left join user_role ur on ur.user_id = u.user_id left join role r on r.role_id = ur.role_id left join employee e on e.employee_id = u.employee_id
order by u.user_id desc limit #{limit} offset #{offset}

select count(*) from sys_user u join user_role ur on ur.user_id = u.user_id join role r on r.role_id = ur.role_id where r.role_name = 'ADMIN' and u.status = 1 and u.user_id <> #{userId,jdbcType=INTEGER}
